local_review.finding_body: FS-test-contract.2.1 forbids test-side reflection that bypasses the library behavior a consumer can invoke. tests/src/org.mongodb/mongodb-driver-core/5.7.0/src/test/java/org_mongodb/mongodb_driver_core/DirectBufferDeallocatorInnerJava8DeallocatorTest.java uses getDeclaredClasses, getDeclaredField, getDeclaredMethod, setAccessible, Unsafe.allocateInstance, and direct private-field mutation to manufacture DirectBufferDeallocator$Java8Deallocator execution on the JDK 25 lanes. The normal public constructor selects the Java 9 implementation there. I could not safely rewrite the scenario without that bypass; removing it would delete an inherited passing scenario and may reduce the reported 13/13 dynamic-access coverage. A maintainer must decide how to make or retire this historical coverage without violating the contribution contract.
local_review.finding_title: Test-side reflection forces an unreachable implementation path
local_review.fix_note: Raised all explicit connection, read, server-selection, and operation timeouts in ByteBufBsonArrayTest and SocketStreamHelperTest to the required 10-second minimum, updating the corresponding assertions. The exact Forge finalization command completed successfully afterward and made no further publishable change.
local_review.review_comment: Reviewed the complete coordinate-scoped diff, local gate evidence, compile-signature adaptation, metadata format, index integrity, test behavior, security-sensitive operations, and old/new dynamic-access statistics. Overall and reflection coverage both remain 13/13 (100%). The Forge-owned finalization command then passed all three native lanes, metadata validation, style checks, generated-test checks, and statistics generation without further publishable changes. The contribution still requires maintainer intervention because DirectBufferDeallocatorInnerJava8DeallocatorTest directly reflects into and unsafe-allocates MongoDB implementation classes to force the Java 8 deallocator path, contrary to FS-test-contract.2.1. A compliant local rewrite that preserves this scenario is not evident on the JDK 25 test lanes, while deleting it would weaken inherited coverage and violate the repair constraints.
